newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda shilling loses ground at end coffee season.
newsitem.headline: Uganda shilling loses ground at end coffee season.

text.p: The Ugandan shilling has weakened by nearly five percent against the dollar since April 11, Central Bank of Uganda (BOU) officials said on Friday.
Walugembe Musoke, acting spokesman for the bank, said this was in line with the end of the coffee season, which usually causes excess demand for dollars.
"The market was hit by some excess demand for dollars because the coffee season is tapering off," he said.
The second coffee quarter, the peak coffee season, ended last month.

The dollar interbank rate on April 4 was 1030 shillings. The shilling had weakened to 1041.77 by April 11 and to 1077.33 by April 25. It stood at 1095 to the dollar on April 25 before recovering slightly to 1090 on April 29.
Central Bank officials said dollar supply was coming down while demand remained fairly high.
"Generally, the demand also dips at around this time, which has not been the case this time," Walugembe said.
The bank officials, however, said the trend was seasonal, as reflected in 1994/95 and 1995/96 financial years.
"It therefore does not represent instability. The depreciation is around five percent," Walugembe said.
